flows.caption: Open your organisation's PeopleOS address. Enter your work e-mail and password, then Sign in.
Forgot password? opens this page. Enter your work e-mail and click Send email.
PeopleOS confirms without saying whether the address exists. The link in the e-mail lets you choose a new password.
Avatar menu › Account security: change your password and set up the authenticator app.
Typing a new password asks for your current password too, before Save changes.
Home: the rail on the left, search, Actions, New and your initials at the top, your work in the middle.
View as Administration: governance items and decisions for the organisation administrator.
View as People operations: the HR team's view of the same Home.
View as Payroll: the payroll team's view.
View as Company: the leadership view.
Review on a decision opens it beside Home, so you can decide without leaving the page.
On a phone, the same Home with a bottom bar.
Admin › All modules: every module you can open, by area.
The area bar's All in … menu lists every module of the area; star the ones you use most.
The area bar on a payroll page: the current module first, then the others of the area.
Ctrl K opens search: recent and suggested pages before you type.
Typing filters actions, pages and people as you type.
Actions lists every action you may start, by module.
New starts something: the most common actions first.
The bell lists your notifications; mark them read or clear them.
Your initials open the avatar menu: Account security, Preferences, theme and Sign out.
Preferences: how Home opens and other personal choices.
Ask PeopleOS explains with sources; it never decides for you.
Press ? for the keyboard shortcuts.
Views on a list: ready-made presets, and Save this view… for your own filters.
Click your initials, then Sign out.
You are back on the sign-in page; this browser's session has ended.
Now: the person's current status and what is next for them.
Journey: every stage of the lifecycle with its dates.
Work: position, team, manager and relationships.
Growth: performance, goals, learning, skills and career.
Rewards: pay and compensation, shown only with the matching permission.
Documents: documents, letters, communications and transitions.
Records: the detailed records, in tabs.
Records › Timeline: every change in date order.
Records › Employment: positions and reporting lines with their dates.
The attendance calendar of one employee: each day's status in its colour.
Process dates turns punches and approved corrections into attendance records.
Run attendance takes a month step by step: absences, arrears, then processing every day.
Paid days with one employee's breakdown for the month.
A holiday calendar and its holidays.
A leave type: Earned leave and its settings.
Apply on behalf: choose the employee, the type and the dates; the balance is shown before you submit.
Adjust a balance: days (+ or −) and a note, posted to the ledger.
Encash leave for an employee: a short wizard.
A new salary component starts with its identity: name, code and type.
The salary structure builder, step 1: name and start date.
Step 2: how pay is set.
Step 3: pick components from a list, or write them in plain English.
Step 4: check the structure on a sample CTC.
Step 5: save as a draft or send for approval.
A structure and its versions: draft, submitted, approved.
Assign salary: the structure, CTC and fixed amounts, with a preview.
Upload salaries in bulk from a CSV file.
A one-time payroll adjustment for an employee and month.
Hold an employee's salary for a month, with a reason.
Payroll uploads: load one-time inputs from a CSV file.
A loan and its instalments, recovered through payroll.
Payroll overview: what to check before you run the month.
Run payroll, step 1: company and pay month, with the month's status.
Step 2: attendance comes first; the banner says what is not ready.
Step 3: pre-payroll checks; tick each group once you have looked at it.
Step 4: what blocks the run is listed with the run's totals.
A month that has not started yet: Start creates its payroll run.
Validate is refused while employees have blocking exceptions; nothing changes.
October, step 2: Process attendance (an administrator with attendance rights).
Attendance processed for the month.
Step 3: each group of changes is ticked with Mark as checked; a group changed after ticking asks to be checked again.
If something is not ready, step 4 lists it: here, checks not ticked and employees without a salary.
Ready to calculate: Calculate, or Calculate in background for large months.
Calculate asks to confirm: existing results are replaced.
Step 5: the totals of the calculated month, ready to validate.
Validate checks for blocking exceptions.
Approve is offered to someone other than the person who ran the payroll.
Approve with a note.
Approved and ready to close.
Before approving, open employees' breakdowns: each line with its basis.
The Payroll Auditor lists findings to look at before approval.
Recalculate re-reads the inputs after a correction.
Step 6: Close payroll.
Closing locks the month's attendance and inputs and prepares the payslips; it can be reopened until it is marked paid or a return is filed.
Step 7: Publish payslips.
Publishing shows each employee their payslip on the web and the app.
Payslips of the closed month.
A payslip.
Step 8: download the bank file and the journal voucher, then Mark as paid once the bank has paid.
Mark as paid: after this the month can no longer be reopened.
The closed run in Payroll runs.
The closed run's More menu.

warnings_first.title: The pictures that follow: a month taken to the end
warnings_first.headline: Approve, close, publish and pay open only once PeopleOS has verified the statutory rules your run uses.
warnings_first.body: In the example organisation those rules are not yet verified, so its runs stop at Validate. To show the rest of the month, the next pictures come from a copy of the example organisation where that check was switched off.
points: Everything else on these screens is exactly what you will see.
In your organisation, ask PeopleOS support if a run stops on unverified statutory rules.
warnings_first.todo: Treat any 'not verified' warning in these pictures as a blocker in your own runs.
